title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Nvidia board weighs ousting CEO Jensen Huang
preheader: Kushner and Witkoff fly to Putin; six killed in a strike on a Gaza hospital.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Thursday, November 12, 2026 — the 2 stories that matter most today, plus 1 update on stories you're following and 8 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Nvidia's board prepares to remove CEO Jensen Huang, reports say
stories.why_important: US media reported this week that Nvidia's board is weighing whether to remove CEO Jensen Huang. He has admitted an affair with a woman in business whom US spy agencies link to Beijing. Nvidia's chips drive the AI boom, so his exit would shake markets and US-China tech policy.
stories.what_overlooked: The reported second affair involves an Nvidia employee, giving directors a work conduct case separate from the China spying question.
stories.prediction: A board statement by Friday would show whether directors act on the affairs alone or on the FBI's China inquiry.

stories.story_title: Israeli strike on Khan Younis hospital kills six, Gaza medics say
stories.why_important: An airstrike hit a building at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis before dawn Thursday. It killed at least six people, including a surgeon, and wounded about 20. Israel said it targeted a senior Hamas commander working inside the hospital.
stories.what_overlooked: Israel says it widened the campaign because Hamas is regrouping and rearming. The toll comes from Gaza's civil defence, not an outside count.
stories.prediction: Whether Nasser Hospital's remaining wards still treat patients next week will show how far the campaign is squeezing Gaza's health care.

quick_hits.text: Italy, Scotland and Ireland reported similar emailed school bomb threats, and Italy's premier said there was no concrete danger.
Spain's unions staged the first general strike in 14 years, drawing millions to protests over housing three weeks before a snap election.
Democrat Scott Colom beat Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, becoming the state's first Black US senator since 1874.
Indonesia's vice president, Gibran Rakabuming, resigned after courts ruled his overseas education papers did not meet election requirements.
Russia's ambassador to Washington, Alexander Darchiev, died suddenly in Moscow at 66 from an unspecified chronic illness.
Kenya's education ministry records show some registered schools with no learners and pupils who cannot be traced to a classroom.
Haiti's prime minister praised El Salvador's military after a joint strike on a suspected home of a 400 Mawozo gang leader.
Iran's security chief said military bases from West Asia to Europe would be 'legitimate targets' if the US restarts the war.

big_number.context: Schools across Italy got the same emailed bomb threat on Wednesday, as Europe faced a wave of hoaxes and cyberattacks.
